title: Recurse application manifest
description: The `agent.yaml` manifest declares a complete Recurse application: its identity, runtime, agent behavior, run input and output schemas, and tools. The shape is closed; unknown fields are rejected.

kind.description: The kind of application this manifest declares. Always `Agent`.

metadata.description: Identity of the application shown to its callers.

name.description: Stable application identifier. Also used as the deployed tool name.

summary.description: One-sentence description of what the application does. Also used as the deployed tool description.
examples: Tunes a tiny classifier across feature and training configurations.

runtime.description: The Python runtime the application executes in.

lockfile.description: The lockfile that pins the application's dependencies. Always `uv.lock`, generated by uv from the application's `pyproject.toml`; both files must be present and consistent.

agent.description: The agent that drives the application's tools: its system prompt, optional model selection, and optional reliability limits.

model.description: Specialist model identifier. Omit to use the current service default. The service checks availability and pricing during preparation; unsupported or unavailable models are rejected without substitution. Preparation records the resolved selection, so existing deployments do not change when the default changes.

prompt.description: Relative path to the agent's system prompt file.

max_llm_errors.description: Consecutive model errors tolerated before the run stops. `0` disables this limit.

max_tool_errors.description: Consecutive tool batches in which every call fails, tolerated before the run stops; any successful call resets the count. `0` disables this limit.

timeout_tools.description: Timeout in seconds applied to each application tool call. `0` and `null` disable the timeout.

inputs.description: JSON Schema (Draft 2020-12) describing run inputs. Supplied values are validated against it and property defaults are applied. The resolved `task` string, templated with `{{ input.NAME }}` placeholders, becomes the agent task; the remaining values are available to tools through `recurse.context().inputs`.

outputs.description: Self-contained JSON Schema (Draft 2020-12) describing the structured object returned by a successful run and exposed as the deployed MCP tool output schema.

type.description: A successful run always returns one JSON object.

tools.description: The application's tool module and tool registrations.

source.description: Relative path to the Python module that defines the tools. Every public module-level function must be registered.

built_in.description: Whether Recurse's built-in agent tools are also registered. Defaults to true.

defaults.description: Default behavior settings applied to every registered tool. Per-tool settings override them.

register.description: Tools to expose, keyed by public function name in `tools.source`. Each value is `~` (use defaults) or a mapping with the same keys as `tools.defaults`.

toolSettings.description: Optional behavior declarations for a registered tool.

no_storage.description: Parameter names for which the optional stored-object reference alternative is removed. This does not relax type requirements: in Recurse's strict mode, Any, including values inside dict[str, Any] or list[Any], still requires stored-object references. Use concrete types for inline data. Names must exist in the tool signature. Defaults to an empty list.

pure_args.description: Parameter names the tool guarantees not to mutate. Names must exist in the tool signature. Omit or use an empty list for conservative behavior; null declares all parameters pure.

volatile.description: Whether repeated calls with the same arguments may return different results. Defaults to false.

storable.description: Whether results may be stored and passed between tools by reference. When omitted, Recurse infers it from the tool's return type.
